meta.title: dsh-mcp-manager
meta.description: Manage MCP servers, choose when allowed servers load, and filter the tools available to a session.

en.mcp.list.title: Server list
en.mcp.mode.dynamic.desc: MCP is not loaded at session start; it is inserted into the system tool list once needed. That breaks the cache prefix once, and argument calls stay more stable.
en.mcp.mode.eager.desc: The original behavior: at session start every started MCP and its tools load into the system tool list, and filtering individual tools is not supported.
en.mcp.mode.lazy.desc: MCP is not loaded at session start; it is inserted into context once needed. The cache prefix survives, and it costs fewer tokens.
en.mcp.mode.saveFailed: The loading mode was not saved; the list still shows the last setting that took effect.
en.mcp.mode.title: MCP loading
en.mcp.noMatch.hint: Try another term, or clear the filter box.
en.mcp.page.intro: Manage the available MCP servers, when they enter the context, and how much of a tool list one call hands to the model.
en.mcp.page.title: MCP
en.mcp.readonly.composedRow: The composition or a patch layer declares this row, not your own Include file, so the settings page cannot switch or edit it. Move the row into your own Include file to change it here.
en.mcp.readonly.noInclude: This composition mounts no file-backed Include of your own, so global rows cannot be switched or edited from the settings page. Declare them in an Include row inside your own composition file.
en.mcp.readonly.severalIncludes: Several writable file-backed Includes are mounted, so it is unclear which file owns this row; the settings page cannot switch or edit it.
en.mcp.readonly.unreadableInclude: The one writable Include file could not be read, so this row cannot be confirmed as one of its rows; the settings page cannot switch or edit it.
en.mcp.row.toggleFailed: The switch did not take effect:
en.mcp.search.label: Filter servers by name or description
en.mcp.tabs.label: MCP settings sections
en.opt.annotations.desc: Carry the server's read-only / destructive / idempotent / open-world hints in a listing, so the model can tell which operations change data before it calls one.
en.opt.catalog.empty: No server catalogue yet. A record appears once the model loads or searches a server.
en.opt.catalog.title: Catalogue state
en.opt.catalogTtl.desc: Zero disables reuse and reconnects on every search. A shorter ttlMs published by the server wins over this value, and a tools/list_changed notification invalidates that server immediately.
en.opt.group.annotations.hint: MCP annotations are server claims, and the spec requires clients to treat them as untrusted, so they are shown as hints only.
en.opt.group.catalog.hint: How long a discovery result stays usable; a cache hit means a search starts no process at all.
en.opt.group.load.hint: How much one call puts into the context.
en.opt.group.search.hint: Find tools by what they do without loading a server.
en.opt.hideDestructive.desc: Removes tools whose annotations.destructiveHint is true from the session's visible set: neither registered nor callable. Only an explicit declaration counts, tools without annotations are unaffected, and an already-loaded server is not changed retroactively — the next load applies it.
en.opt.maxTools.desc: How many tools one paginated tools/list walk may collect, so an enormous server cannot flood the context or memory. A listing cut short is marked truncated; the tools beyond the cap are collected nowhere and no query can reach them — only a higher cap reveals them.
en.opt.namesOnly.desc: With this on, mcp_load omits argument schemas by default; when the model decides to call one tool it fetches that tool's full arguments with mcp_load's `tool` parameter. Off, every listing carries the full schemas.
en.opt.pageSize.desc: How many tools mcp_load and mcp_search list at once. A longer listing carries a nextCursor, so the model can page through a large server instead of pulling every tool into the context at once.
en.opt.save.notWritable: The MCP settings document is not writable; nothing was saved.
en.opt.search.desc: Registers mcp_search, which matches keywords against every discovered MCP tool and returns only the matching names with a one-line description — no argument schemas in the context. Without it the model has to guess which server to load.
en.opt.searchIndex.desc: A search may connect to servers it has no tool list for (at most 3 at a time, 8 seconds each) and record the result. With this off, a search only answers for already-cached servers and names the ones it could not look inside, so the model loads those first.
